title: Live on CrazyGames under two weeks after day 1, made with Claude and SpriteCook
author: beto-deoliveira
selftext:
AI disclosure: I made this with AI tools. The pixel art is made with SpriteCook and the code with Claude. The idea, the design and the testing are mine.

Tummy Turbo is live: [https://www.crazygames.com/game/tummy-turbo](https://www.crazygames.com/game/tummy-turbo)

Tummy Turbo is a silly vertical runner where you mix your own fuel.

Pick up to 3 foods and eat. The gas launches Gus straight up, through the street, the clouds, space and beyond.

I shared day 1 here a week ago. This is how it got from there to here:

* Claude Code wrote the code (Phaser 4). The idea, the design, the testing and every call are mine.
* SpriteCook made the pixel art, in about 50 small batches. Every new Gus sprite starts from the one I approved, so he stays the same.
* All the sound and music is made in code. There are no audio files.
* My feedback became a checklist. Claude checks every change against it before showing me, so I only say a thing once.
* Before each upload, a script plays the built game in a headless browser and checks the portal's rules.
* The preview video is cut in code with Remotion.

The plan changed late. The first portal I picked wasn't taking new developers. Switching to CrazyGames took one day: their SDK, saves on the player's account, the covers and the preview video.

Biggest lesson: the AI is fast. My job became saying clearly what's wrong, then turning it into a rule.

Which part of the workflow would you want a deeper post on?

Follow me at r/TummyTurbo for more.
